narrative: Markets experienced a broad-based rally across equities as dip-buying returned, with both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq trading near session highs despite an investigation into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Investors rotated into semiconductor peers such as AMD and broader AI plays, treating Nvidia's decline as company-specific key-man risk. Crude oil plummeted sharply, with WTI dropping over 4-5% and Brent falling 7%, which helped fuel equity optimism. Meanwhile, gold pushed higher alongside equity gains. Macro focus remains centered on tomorrow's CPI print—the final reading before the Fed's early December decision—amid expectations of another potential rate hike by year-end and Washington political uncertainty following impeachment articles introduced against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Nasdaq.why: The index surged 3.4% led by a strong rebound in semiconductor stocks and broader AI demand, shrugging off a 5% drop in Nvidia.

S&P 500.why: Trading near session highs with broad-based participation as all 11 industry groups finished higher, led by industrials.

Gold.why: Advanced $33.49 an ounce to trade at $4,103 according to show anchors.

Oil.why: Suffered a steep selloff with WTI dropping over 4-5% to $87.50 and Brent plunging 7% to $93.40.
